briefing.summary: Descend to the Leggo lander's 2014 bait-station site on the floor of the Eastern Pool, then climb the steep north inner wall of the trench. The near-site start skips the first 6 km of descent and leaves nearly 5 km to explore.
facts: The Challenger Deep's Eastern Pool is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans; the deepest cell surveyed in this tile is 10,930.9 m.
This full-ocean-depth hull is rated to 11,000 m, clearing the deepest terrain in this mission.
First crewed descent: Trieste, 23 January 1960 (Jacques Piccard, Don Walsh). Most recent well-instrumented survey used here: the Five Deeps Expedition's DSV Limiting Factor, 2019.
Nothing lives here that you can see with the naked eye except hadal amphipods (Hirondellea gigas) at bait -- no fish have been confirmed this deep.
hazards: Rated depth: 11,000 m. The deepest terrain in this mission is 10,931 m; the hull warning begins beyond its rating.
Total darkness below a few hundred metres; only your lights work.
With a surface start, expect a long descent from the 6,000 m spawn; the default near-site start skips it.
Extreme, uniform pressure (about 1,086 bar at the bottom) and near-freezing water (1-4 degC).

objectives.title: Scan the Leggo lander's amphipod bait site
objectives.hint: The Leggo lander site is on the Eastern Pool floor, near 10,925 m.

objectives.title: Survey the steep north inner wall
objectives.hint: The north inner wall rises northwest of the Leggo site, near 9,980 m.

objectives.title: Cross to the Central Pool, the trench's second basin
objectives.hint: Follow the trench axis far west from the Eastern Pool to the Central Pool, near 10,930 m.

objectives.title: Find the sill separating the Central and Eastern Pools
objectives.hint: The higher sill along the trench axis lies west of the Eastern Pool, between it and the Central Pool, near 10,700 m.
